simple.meaning: מַלְכָּא (malkâʼ) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a queen.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Daniel 5:10. The surrounding context includes family line, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַלְכָּא (H4433) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

firstOccurrence.englishText: The queen by reason of the words of the king and his lords came into the banquet house. The queen spoke and said, “O king, live forever; don’t let your thoughts trouble you, nor let your face be changed.
